rationale: Banned tolokers are organic fraud actors on a crowdsourcing platform, not injected outliers: a banned worker is someone who farms tasks with template/minimal profile statistics that look maximally ordinary. feature_dup_rate = 0.489 with only feature_dim = 10 and feature_sparsity = 0.48 means the attribute matrix is template-dominated, so the ban signal sits among feature-space in-liers, not outliers. This is exactly the camouflage-by-conformity regime, and conformity's landmarker confirms a mass of near-saturated in-liers (p50 = 0.870, mean = 0.811) rather than a thin outlier tail, so it leads. attr_struct_mismatch is the complementary cross-modal view and shows the best-separated upper tail of the label-free landmarkers (p50 = 0.314 to p95 = 0.799, p99 = 0.914, std = 0.245): a worker whose profile statistics read normal while their co-task structure does not is the signature of a banned account hiding behind a clean profile. local_affinity is justified by homophily = 0.749, high enough that genuine neighbour agreement is the norm, and its tail separates (p50 = 0.198 to p99 = 0.697); it catches banned workers whose performance statistics diverge from the co-workers they share tasks with. community adds the structural view that neither attribute paradigm covers: modularity = 0.519 over 26 communities with clustering_coeff = 0.533 means the 13 projects induce genuine task-cohorts, and a ban is a project-level event, so poor adherence to any cohort (p90 = 0.544, p99 = 0.734) is a meaningful independent signal. Excluded: density is degenerate here (p50 = p90 = p95 = 0.0, mean = 0.0023), so kNN/LOF has no usable resolution at avg_degree = 88 and density = 0.015; one_class and reconstruction both assume anomalies are hard to reconstruct or fall outside the normal boundary, which is the opposite of the conformity regime this feature matrix implies; spectral is weak (p90 = 0.300) and spectral_gap = 0.132 with is_power_law = false gives no high-frequency story; homophily_violation is largely redundant with local_affinity and attr_struct_mismatch; adversarial adds variance without a distinct assumption.

Domain: a banned toloker is a worker whose profile/performance statistics sit outside the envelope of legitimate work behaviour (rushed tasks, degenerate answer patterns, throwaway or templated profiles), while still being densely connected to ordinary workers because edges only mean 'worked on the same task'. That domain reading drives the choice. (1) one_class: with only feature_dim = 10 dense profile/performance attributes, the normal workforce occupies a compact region and bans are defined by behaviour falling outside it, not by who you co-worked with; an SVDD boundary on the joint embedding is the paradigm whose assumption literally matches 'banned in one of the projects'. The structure carries little of the signal here (density = 0.015, avg_degree = 88.3, clustering_coeff = 0.533: co-task edges are near-random crowds, so purely structural paradigms mostly measure project size). (2) conformity: feature_dup_rate = 0.489 with feature_sparsity = 0.480 on a 10-dim profile vector means a large mass of workers share identical templated profiles, exactly the camouflage case; its landmarker is the only one with a mass-dominated response (mean 0.811, p50 0.870), i.e. the template regime is really present, and its NEGATIVE-residual reading flags the in-liers that one_class's distance measure will under-rank. Deterministic, so it also stabilises the composition. (3) attr_struct_mismatch: strongest separated upper tail of the label-free landmarkers (p50 0.314 -> p90 0.718 -> p99 0.914, std 0.245), which is the signature of workers whose profile statistics disagree with the company they keep, the cross-modal view neither of the above sees. (4) local_affinity: homophily = 0.749 licenses the neighbour-agreement assumption, and it supplies a structural counterweight so the composition is not purely attribute-driven; its tail is present but modest (p90 0.423, p99 0.697), matching its role as the supporting rather than leading view. Excluded: density is degenerate on this graph (p50 = p90 = p95 = 0.0, so the LOF/kNN mechanism carries no usable ranking at avg_degree 88); community and spectral are redundant with the weak structural signal implied by modularity = 0.519 over 26 project-shaped communities and spectral_gap = 0.132 (the spectral landmarker's flat tail, p90 0.300, confirms it); reconstruction and adversarial would re-encode the same 10-dim attribute view as one_class but with a positive-residual assumption that conformity already contradicts on a template-dominated matrix; homophily_violation overlaps attr_struct_mismatch with a weaker tail.

The task is finding banned crowdworkers: fraudsters/cheaters who survive on the platform precisely by looking like ordinary workers. Node features are only 10 dimensions of profile and performance statistics, with feature_dup_rate 0.489 and feature_sparsity 0.480, i.e. a template-dominated feature matrix where many workers share identical stat vectors. Banned tolokers are therefore feature-space in-liers, not outliers, which is exactly the camouflage-by-conformity regime; the conformity landmarker confirms a dense mass at the conformant end (mean 0.811, p50 0.870) so the mechanism is measurable here. one_class complements it: with only 10 dense dimensions and 11758 nodes, an SVDD boundary on graph embeddings captures the joint profile-plus-performance envelope of legitimate workers rather than per-feature deviation, catching workers whose statistics are individually plausible but jointly off. attr_struct_mismatch adds the cross-modal view that matters for ban detection: a worker whose task-co-occurrence structure (avg_degree 88.3, max_degree 2138, degree_std 161.8, clustering 0.533) disagrees with what their profile statistics claim is the signature of someone farming many tasks under a normal-looking profile; its landmarker has the widest spread of all (std 0.245, p90 0.718, p99 0.914), the strongest separated tail on offer. community covers coordinated or project-specific ban patterns: 26 communities at modularity 0.519 correspond roughly to project/task clusters, and low adherence flags workers who drift across projects without belonging to any, with a decent upper tail (p90 0.544, p99 0.734). I deliberately drop local_affinity and homophily_violation despite homophily 0.749: edges here mean 'worked on the same task', not social endorsement, so neighbor feature agreement is driven by task assignment rather than by legitimacy, and both landmarkers are weakly tailed relative to attr_struct_mismatch. density is unusable (p95 = 0.0, degenerate at density 0.015 with avg_degree 88). Reconstruction and adversarial are skipped as redundant with conformity's residual view on a 10-dimensional template matrix, where an autoencoder's error would be dominated by the duplicated rows.
